title: Beyond the 956: Clem Cattini, Tornados drummer behind 42 No. 1 hits, dies at 89
excerpt: Clem Cattini, the legendary British drummer who co-founded The Tornados and played on 42 UK No. 1 singles, has died at 89. The BBC confirmed his death on November 4, 2026; he died on November 2 after a fall at his home.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Clem Cattini, the legendary British drummer who co-founded The Tornados and played on more UK No. 1 singles than any other British drummer, has died at 89.

Cattini died on Monday, November 2, 2026, after a fall at his home. BBC News confirmed his death on November 4, 2026, as tributes poured in from musicians across the industry.

Born Clemente Anselmo Agustino Cattini in Stoke Newington, London, in August 1937, he began his recording career on Johnny Kidd & the Pirates' “Shakin' All Over,” which topped the UK chart in 1960. In 1961, he co-founded The Tornados, whose Joe Meek-produced instrumental “Telstar” became the first single by a British group to top the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 in 1962.

Cattini went on to become one of Britain's most sought-after session drummers, playing on 42 UK No. 1 singles, including Tom Jones' “Green, Green Grass of Home,” Dusty Springfield's “You Don't Have to Say You Love Me,” and Tony Christie's “(Is This the Way to) Amarillo?” He also recorded with the Bee Gees, Engelbert Humperdinck, Gene Pitney, and Lulu, and played in the BBC orchestra for Top of the Pops.

Tributes came from across the music world. Tony Christie, Donovan, and Carl Palmer of Emerson, Lake & Palmer were among those who remembered him, with Christie calling him “the greatest British session drummer of all time.”

Rest in Peace, Clem Cattini.

Sources: BBC News, confirming his death and tributes; Music Times; Wide Open Country.
